readout_other: Hippocampal EEG spike counting (delta/theta/alpha/gamma bands); resting-state fMRI 36x36 ROI functional connectivity matrix; c-Fos immunohistochemistry; H&E histology
direction_notes: FUS to the ANT reduced PTZ-induced hippocampal EEG spike counts by ~29-42% (low- and high-dose pooled, ~36% overall) and reduced thalamus-hippocampus resting-state functional connectivity (45.1% decrease), normalizing PTZ-induced increases in c-Fos expression in the thalamus-hippocampus circuit.
safety_notes: H&E histology showed no obvious tissue disruption, immune cell infiltration, or microglial activation in cortex, thalamus or hippocampus of FUS-treated animals, indicating FUS did not cause detectable histological damage.

exposures.label: Burst-mode FUS to anterior nucleus of thalamus (low-dose and high-dose ISI protocols)

timing.protocol_description: Burst-mode FUS (0.25 MI, 30% duty cycle) was delivered for a total exposure duration of 600 s (10 min) as 5 on/off cycles: a 'high-dose' protocol of 90-s on periods with 30-s inter-stimulus interval (ISI), and a 'low-dose' protocol of 30-s on periods with 90-s ISI. EEG was recorded 40 min after the end of FUS; spike counts decreased similarly (29-42%) for both dose protocols so they were pooled for connectivity analysis.

source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: In this study, the exposure duration was 600  s with high-dose protocol of 90-sec “on” periods, with 30  s ISI for 5 cycles and low-dose protocol of 30-sec “on” periods, with 90-sec ISI for 5 cycles (ISI = 90).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: A custom focused ultrasound transducer (fundamental frequency = 1  MHz, radius curvature = 16  mm) was attached to a custom-made gel coupler.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: The duty cycle was set to 30% based on previous FUS-epilepsy studies<sup>15,16</sup> which was equivalent to FUS exposure intensities (defined as spatial-peak temporal average, $\bar { \mathrm { I _ { S P T A } ^ { \mathrm { - } } } } )$ of 0.7 W/cm<sup>2</sup>.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: In this study, the exposure duration was 600  s with high-dose protocol of 90-sec “on” periods, with 30  s ISI for 5 cycles and low-dose protocol of 30-sec “on” periods, with 90-sec ISI for 5 cycles (ISI = 90).
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: Variable pulsing paradigms were tested (0.25 mechanical index (MI), 30% duty cycle, spatial-peak temporal average $( \mathrm { I } _ { \mathrm { { S P T A } } } ) { = } 0 . 3 \mathrm { \ : W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ with 30 s inter-stimulus interval (ISI), referred to as “high-dose”, and with 90 s ISI, referred to as “low-dose”) to examine diferent impacts on spike reduction.

flags.reason: Paper gives group-level counts (32 total; 28 received PTZ; histology used Normal n=4, PTZ-alone n=4, PTZ-FUS n=8) but never states how many of the 28 PTZ animals were assigned to the PTZ-FUS (actual FUS-exposed) group for the main EEG/fMRI experiments, so left not_reported.

Abstract and the 'FUS sonication protocol' Results section both state ISPTA = 0.3 W/cm2, but the Methods 'FUS setup and parameters design' section states the same 30% duty cycle 'was equivalent to FUS exposure intensities...of 0.7 W/cm2'; recorded the majority value (0.3) and flag this internal discrepancy.
Paper states MI (0.25) and duty cycle (30%) for the burst-mode FUS but never states a pulse repetition frequency or pulse duration, so both left not_reported (burst rule could not be resolved).
Comparator groups (Normal, PTZ-alone) received no ultrasound exposure at all rather than an inactive-transducer sham, so coded as none with this flag for clarity.
